subject.title: [Feature]: Webhook hook sessions should reuse existing session when sessionKey is consistent (multi-turn support)

question: Should hook-agent traffic get an explicit persistent-session opt-in, and what hook auth and session-key boundaries must gate it before https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75918 can land?
rationale: The implementation changes how external hook requests can re-enter durable agent context, so the permanent API and security boundary need maintainer intent rather than an automatic issue-fix lane.

options.title: Land explicit persistent mode
options.body: Accept a sessionMode: "persistent" opt-in with isolated default behavior, existing hook auth, prefix checks, docs, and regression proof.

options.title: Keep hooks isolated
options.body: Reject persistent hook-agent sessions for now and update docs/API wording so webhook callers do not expect multi-turn continuity.

options.title: Choose a different API shape
options.body: Pause the current PR and specify another compatibility-safe surface such as a narrower session target or trust-scoped binding API.

recommendation.title: Land explicit persistent mode
recommendation.body: Accept a sessionMode: "persistent" opt-in with isolated default behavior, existing hook auth, prefix checks, docs, and regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter already framed the issue-level sessionMode direction and has the strongest review-history signal for the product/security boundary choice.
